# PAPER_PLAN_DEPRECATED — findings parked out of the current paper

**Created 2026-07-28**, when the paper direction returned to the SPARCAL-modality story
([PAPER_PLAN.md](PAPER_PLAN.md), advisor direction 2026-07-28) and away from the 2026-07-18
coverage-control-reanalysis plan.

**Nothing here is retracted.** Every result below is real, reproducible, and was generated by us.
It is parked for one of two reasons:

- **(A) It is the seed of the planned second paper** — a thorough coverage-controlled benchmark of
  the existing spatial-SNV detection tools. Keep, reuse, do not re-run.
- **(B) It actively endangers a claim in the current paper.** These must be *read before writing*:
  they tell you exactly which sentences a reviewer can knock down, and what the safe phrasing is.

`data/spatialsnv_reanalysis_2026-07-17/README.md` holds the full method detail and every CSV; the
2026-07-17/18 blocks in [On_going.md](On_going.md) hold the blow-by-blow.

## 1. (A) The coverage-confound benchmark — the whole of paper #2

### 1.1 Coverage-conditional region test with a working positive control

Logistic `tumor ~ z(log burden) + z(log total UMI)` on pathologist ground truth, plus standalone AUC
(the robust metric under collinearity). Two coverage-independent samples.

**P6 (Ji-2020-derived leading-edge mask; 1,504 tumor / 2,215 normal):**

| predictor | standalone AUC |
|---|---|
| expression, TSK signature | **0.807** |
| coverage (total UMI) | 0.664 |
| MMP10 | 0.637 |
| SPARCAL somatic burden | 0.631 |
| Monopogen burden | 0.570 |
| SpatialSNV burden | 0.55–0.58 |
| STMut burden at gold WES sites | **0.432 (below chance)** |

**DCIS2 (10 pathologist foci / 249 spots, coverage-only AUC 0.913):** epithelial signature 0.946,
ERBB2 0.941, EPCAM 0.907 — all **beat coverage** (coef p = 9e-11 → ~0). Every SNV burden flavour
adds nothing (p = 0.32–0.77), including SpatialSNV's own "effective" and ">20 reads" tiers.

⇒ **Expression beats coverage on both samples; no SNV burden does — for SpatialSNV, Monopogen, STMut
and our own SPARCAL alike.** The positive control proves the test is not rigged to null everything.
CSVs: `p6_axis2_pathology_GT.csv`, `dcis2_axis2_with_poscontrol.csv`.

### 1.2 Published subclone/trajectory structure is coverage-dominated

SpatialSNV, DCIS1+DCIS2: SNV-window PC1 correlates 0.90 with UMI; top-10 PCs reconstruct ~90 % of
UMI variance; KMeans-3 "subclones" are coverage strata (η²(UMI) = 0.71–0.74).
**Boundary:** PC2/PC3 carry minor non-coverage structure (consistent with the Moran's I residual
0.351 on SpatialSNV-private P4 calls) → the defensible claim is *coverage-dominated*, never
*"the subclones are false."* CSV: `ssnv_step3_subclonal_coverage.csv`.

### 1.3 The platform information limit (four independent axes)

1. **Singletons:** 77–87 % of SpatialSNV's calls are single-spot single-molecule (verified over
   4.7 M observations); 61–82 % for ours. Tool-independent.
2. **Callability:** RNA covers ~1 % of WES-somatic DNA positions (P4 40/3,451; P6 27/2,604).
3. **Cross-method non-convergence:** SPARCAL ∩ SpatialSNV Jaccard **0.049** on P6 (6.9–14.6 % mutual
   coverage); ≤0.3 % of either method's calls hit the 14,565-site WES-somatic truth; only **9
   positions (0.06 %)** agreed by all three methods. `p6_crossmethod_jaccard.csv`.
4. **Expression bias:** called genes have ~60× the median UMI of a typical gene; Spearman(#calls per
   gene, gene UMI) = 0.22–0.26. Plus a modest but significant 3′ shift (SPARCAL relative position
   0.528 vs gene-length-matched null 0.499; SpatialSNV 0.547). `p6_3prime_bias_summary.csv`,
   `p6_gene_expression_bias.csv`.

*Axes 1 and 2 are re-used in the current paper as "why somatic is hard" (PAPER_PLAN §3 Story C1).
Axes 3 and 4 stay here.*

### 1.4 STMut extension at gold DNA somatic loci

Per-spot ALT-UMI at 14,565 matched-WES somatic sites, P6: only **20.4 % of spots get any signal**
(median 1 site/spot, max 5); standalone AUC **0.432**, and tumor spots carry *lower* burden than
normal (0.163 vs 0.415). Even at true DNA somatic loci, per-spot somatic-read presence does not mark
the tumor — the confound is in the RNA readout, not in calling errors.
`stmut_p6_extension.csv`, `scripts/postanalyze/stmut_p6_extension.py`.

## 2. (B) ⚠️ Endangers the germline stories

### 2.1 Unbinned SPARCAL vs GATK is a statistical tie
12-section paired Wilcoxon: **p = 0.52** raw, **p = 0.68** binned; mean difference +0.004–0.009, an
order of magnitude below run-to-run standard deviation. The remembered "clear win" is the
**single-section 151507 pilot (0.304 vs 0.184) that did not generalize.**
⇒ PAPER_PLAN §4.1 (promoting `defined` unbinned to 12 sections) is what decides whether the
advisor's Story A has any multi-section support. See [[project_sparcal_vs_gatk_statistical_tie]].

### 2.2 Unbinned SPARCAL never beats gene expression
0/12 sections, both mean and best-run. The draft's "151672: 0.701 vs 0.600" does not reproduce
(current 151672: sparcal 0.148 mean / 0.212 best vs GE 0.540 / 0.740). The "beats GE" panel only
exists for the **250-kb-binned** representation (4/12 sections by mean, 5/12 by best run).

### 2.3 Adding UPV/somatic to the germline set hurts on DLPFC
151507: raw germline (1kG+UPV) 0.177, defsom (1kG+somatic) 0.245, merged 0.160 — all below
`defined` 0.277. Binned: germline 0.317, merged 0.287 below `defined_bin250kb` 0.351.
**UPV, not somatic, is the drag.** The one exception is `defsom_bin250kb` = 0.364 > `defined_bin250kb`
0.332 on 151507 — which is exactly the advisor's Story B point, and exactly the number that has not
been promoted. Its nearest relative, `somtop25_bin250kb`, **lost on promotion** (0.350 vs 0.363;
its single-section 0.364 turned out to be seed noise). Treat the single-section `defsom` win as
*unconfirmed* until §4.2 runs. See [[project_dlpfc_snv_representation_study]].

### 2.4 Everything else in the representation sweep failed
TF-IDF 0.186, SVG-select 0.117–0.148, VAF/rawbin 0.129–0.137, prevalence-cap 0.111–0.155,
exome-restriction 0.094–0.148, floor sweep ~neutral, `floor20∘somtop25` 0.317 — all at or below
baseline. **Only genomic binning wins**, and it lifts *every* caller by ~+0.14 ARI, so it is a
representation result, not a SPARCAL result. Further variant-selection tweaking on DLPFC is
low-yield; do not spend time there.

### 2.5 The DLPFC ARI "regression" and the dedup ablation
The 0.28 → 0.21 drop is **code drift** (the germline set grew ~27 % from the same BAMs), not UMI
dedup. Dedup is **ARI-neutral** (~+0.01, same-code matched). **Do not write "dedup hurts normal
tissue" in the paper** — the old "0.29 vs 0.20" claim was confounded.
See [[project_dlpfc_ari_regression_codedrift]], [[project_umi_dedup_ablation_finding]].

## 3. (B) ⚠️ Endangers the COSMIC cascade (PAPER_PLAN §3 Story C3)

### 3.1 Superseded COSMIC framing

**User decision (2026-09-06):** retain COSMIC as a same-basis external catalogue comparison across
classes and callers. The paper reports raw and xMHC-excluded summaries consistently and does not use
catalogue membership as variant-level validation or evidence that individual calls are
cancer-driving. Historical analysis code and result tables remain available as provenance but no
additional COSMIC model or control panel is scheduled.

**Safe phrasing:** the cascade separates the classes; UPV > somatic is consistent with UPV containing
truncal/early somatic. **Unsafe:** "COSMIC enrichment validates our somatic calls as cancer-relevant."

### 3.2 The cascade does not reproduce on the `pre_dedup` sets
somatic/unresolved ratio: P4 **0.95× (p = 0.71)**, P6 **0.92× (ns)**, DCIS1 **1.06× (ns)** — i.e.
null. The published-looking numbers (1.16–1.33×) are from the `current` post-dedup sets, which are
~6× larger partly through known **code drift**. The two "co-headline" axes of the old plan were
computed on *inconsistent* versions (COSMIC on `current`, region tests on `pre_dedup`).
⇒ PAPER_PLAN Decision **D1**: lock one version for the whole paper.
Baseline: `data/set_benchmark/baseline_pre_dedup/scorecard.csv`.

### 3.3 HLA drives the DCIS effect entirely
Excluding chr6:28–34 Mb: P4 1.33× → 1.22× (p = 4.2e-3, holds), P6 1.29× → 1.18× (p = 1.1e-3, holds),
DCIS1 1.16× → 1.11× (p = 0.099, marginal), **DCIS2 1.17× → 0.99× (p = 0.55, gone)**. Biologically
sensible — UV-hypermutated cSCC vs low-TMB early DCIS. **Framing must be tumor-type-specific, never
"all four samples."**

### 3.4 A somatic-vs-1kG COSMIC test is meaningless
1kG is *common-variant*, and COSMIC `GenomeScreensMutant` is polluted with germline from
unmatched-normal tumor screens. Comparing somatic against 1kG only reproduces that confound, and a
matched null cannot flip a reversed ordering. **Do not build a somatic-vs-1kG or random-loci null.**
The within-denovo contrast (somatic vs unresolved) is the only well-posed variant-level test.

### 3.5 The SComatic PON/RNA-editing mask does not help
Ratio moved 1.327 → 1.170 (P4), 1.292 → 1.127 (P6), 1.161 → **1.324** (DCIS1), 1.170 → **1.000**
(DCIS2) — incoherent across samples. P4/P6 WES-overlapping somatic sites fell 7 → 4 and 7 → 6. And
**61 % of 1KGP-defined sites overlap the external PON**, which rules out coordinate-only removal
outright. **Do not adopt the mask.** Also: COSMIC is a DNA cancer catalogue, not an RNA-artifact
catalogue — the mask experiment gives no evidence that our COSMIC-matched calls are artifacts.
`data/artifact_mask_benchmark/current_scomatic/`, `scripts/postanalyze/apply_artifact_masks.py`.

## 4. (B) ⚠️ Endangers the region-detection story (PAPER_PLAN §3 Story C4)

### 4.1 Coverage alone beats every SNV method on DCIS2
`coverage_only` raw ARI **0.657** / F1 0.807 ≥ best SNV set (merged 0.629 / 0.787). After
coverage-normalization the SNV signal collapses to ~0.10–0.31. The number sits in the same CSV the
figure is built from (`benchmark_norm_bestARI.csv`), so omitting it from the panel is an editorial
choice, not an absence of data. Have the answer prepared.

### 4.2 The somatic coefficient is never robustly positive
Coverage-controlled logistic across P4 / P6 / DCIS1 / DCIS2 under both burden versions: null or
negative everywhere. The single positive (DCIS2 pathology gold, `current`, coef +0.574, p = 0.029)
is unadjusted for multiplicity, not reproduced pre-dedup (+0.065, p = 0.77), and contradicted by
every silver run. `data/somatic_validation_2026-07-13/AXIS2_CNV_CONSENSUS_RESULT.md`.

**Bound on the silver extension:** the copyKAT silver GT is itself near-perfectly coverage-predicted
for P4/DCIS1 (coverage-only AUC 0.986–0.988), so those tests are near-degenerate. The genuinely
coverage-independent tests are DCIS2 pathology gold and P6 (coverage AUC 0.413/0.664). Large negative
germline/UPV silver coefficients are multicollinearity/suppression artifacts (burden ~ UMI r ≈ 0.8–0.94)
— **do not interpret their sign.**

### 4.3 The "5-tool CNV consensus" is one tool
Verified, not assumed: inferCNV (`infercnv_annotations.txt` and its HMM `cell_groupings`) and siCNV
(`*_copykat_annotations.tsv`) are **100.0 % identical to copyKAT** on all four samples — Weiman's
pipeline seeds them with copyKAT labels. numbat and clonalScope have no parseable per-spot label.
So "consensus" = copyKAT (calibration vs DCIS2 pathology: recall 0.924, precision 0.627, F1 0.747).
⚠️ `copyKAT/DCIS_2/P6_Visium_rep1_copykat_prediction.txt` is **misnamed DCIS2 data** — never use it
as P6. The real P6 labels are `copyKAT/P6_rep1_hg38/prediction_aligned.txt`, and copyKAT disagrees
with the P6 pathology mask anyway (F1 0.40) → prefer the mask.

## 5. (B) ⚠️ Endangers method-novelty claims

### 5.1 Artifact-v2 evidence layer: NO-GO at its own pre-locked gate
Job 12576564, DCIS2 pathology clip, repeated stratified 5-fold CV: UMI-only AUC **0.9127**;
UMI + raw somatic alt-UMI **0.9128** (**+0.0001**, ~200× smaller than the CV sd — an exact null).
Worse, the `read_evidence_pass` subset **underperforms** all-somatic raw (0.5236 vs 0.5952) — the
screen removes what little signal exists. UMI-normalized somatic is **below chance** (0.4559).
Root cause is measured, not speculative: 61–82 % of somatic candidates are one alt UMI in one spot.
**The artifact-v2 / spatial-filter-upgrade track is closed. Do not tune thresholds, run all-site
extraction, or start the beta-binomial/HMRF rebuild.**
`data/artifact_evidence_benchmark/v2_dcis2_pathology_2026-07-16/`.

### 5.2 Genotype correction is unvalidated — do not claim it
Matched-normal WES audit (DP ≥ 10, GQ ≥ 20, exact REF/ALT, outside 1KGP): only **131 P4 / 143 P6**
callable sites; raw RNA GT agreement **51.1 % / 55.9 %**; NN predicted-class agreement **51.9 % /
52.4 %**. The classifier writes a predicted class into INFO and selects class-specific VCFs but
**never replaces the `GT` field** — it is a confidence/filtering layer, not a corrected-genotype
caller. Also: PCA in the classifier is dimensionality reduction, not allele transformation; and the
sequence-error gate is a coarse low-BAF/low-depth threshold from Beagle genotype shifts (it labels
13.7 % / 13.4 % of non-reference records as error, **entirely** from the heterozygous class, zero
homozygous). `data/genotype_validation/unseen_normal_wes/{P4,P6}/`,
`scripts/postanalyze/validate_unseen_genotypes.py`.

### 5.3 The BAF-GMM UPV sub-filter (step 7c) is not a reportable result
PURITY_CORR is empirically uninformative *within* UPV (clipped ≥0 and flat, because UPV is
ubiquitous by definition) → the filter is effectively BAF-only. dcis1's 739 low-BAF candidates are
most likely ASE-skewed germline hets, not somatic. dcis2/P4/P6 returned 0. Exploratory only.

### 5.4 The PON ablation says nothing about SPARCAL vs SComatic
It establishes only that a coordinate-only external scRNA PON is not portable as a blanket Visium
filter. The defensible sentence is: *SPARCAL runs without matched controls, whereas PON-aware
filtering is optional and must be validated as a platform/tissue-matched module.* No accuracy claim
without a matched head-to-head.

### 5.5 Axis 3 (sub-clonal agreement) was never run
Blocked on Weiman: numbat's per-spot clone posterior never finished (only bulk `segs_consensus` /
`bulk_clones` exist), and clonalScope's labels are `.rds`-only. Given §5.1's singleton finding it
has a low prior. Not in the current paper; optional for paper #2.
